content.title: About
content.content: Commercial multigrain bread is a whole‑grain loaf made from a blend of wheat, rye, barley, oats and sunflower seeds. It has a dense crumb, nutty aroma and a slight tang, suitable for long‑term storage and large‑scale production.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Multigrain bread typically contains 5–7 different grains and seeds, boosting its nutritional profile.
Traditionally it is baked in industrial ovens at 220 °C, producing an even crust.
Fiber content in 100 g usually exceeds 6 g, higher than in standard white bread.
Fermented starters are often added, enhancing flavor and shelf life.
In many countries the bread is recommended as part of a healthy diet by nutrition guidelines.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestion, promotes satiety and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Grains provide thiamine, riboflavin and niacin, which are essential for energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Contains minerals
items.content: The loaf supplies magnesium, phosphorus and iron, important for muscle function and blood formation.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Mixed grains slow carbohydrate absorption, beneficial for weight management and glucose control.

items.title: Healthy plant oils
items.content: Sunflower and flax seeds add beneficial polyunsaturated fatty acids.

items.title: Grain allergies
items.content: Some individuals may react to wheat, rye or seed components.

items.title: Gluten content
items.content: Not suitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Salt and preservatives
items.content: Commercial versions often contain added salt and preservatives, so intake should be monitored.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Despite its benefits, the bread is energy‑dense; portions should be moderate.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the bread plain, as sandwiches, toasted, or alongside soups and salads. It pairs well with low‑fat cheeses, vegetable spreads and avocado.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place in a paper bag or bread box. For longer storage, freeze wrapped in plastic. Allow to thaw at room temperature before use.
